disease_label_per_paper: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome (Streptococcus pyogenes emm1; CDC-confirmed STSS) with left chest/abdominal wall phlegmon, fatal within 12 hours
presentation_summary: 36-year-old woman with chronic leukopenia since 2017 and prior breast reduction surgery presented with 3 days of fever, chills, diarrhea, vomiting, burning left-sided chest pain radiating toward the abdomen, and dyspnea; denied headache and photophobia; spouse recently had an upper respiratory infection.

Arrival: conscious and oriented, no meningeal signs or focal deficits; HR 124, BP 65/44 mmHg, SpO2 90% on room air; lungs clear; diffuse abdominal tenderness; phlegmon and bullae over the left thoracic and abdominal wall.

Admission labs: CRP 453.04 mg/L, PCT 19.38 ng/mL, urea 10.84 mmol/L, creatinine 240 umol/L, CK 10.34 ukat/L, WBC 2.39 x10^9/L (neutrophils 74.4%, lymphocytes 9.9%, monocytes 0.8%, eosinophils 1.7%, basophils 0), INR 1.44; SOFA components PaO2/FiO2 208.5, platelets 113 x10^3/uL, GCS 13-14, bilirubin 9.28 umol/L.

Imaging: admission chest X-ray without infiltrates; abdominal US sigmoid/descending colitis changes; CT at 2 h: large left pulmonary infiltrate, bilateral pleural effusions, left axillary lymphadenopathy, left thoracic/abdominal wall phlegmon, early ischemic changes in liver, spleen and kidneys.

clinical_course_record.finding: Refractory hypotension on norepinephrine >0.2 ug/kg/min plus vasopressin; progressive oliguric AKI; hypoglycemia; lower-extremity sensory impairment (spine MRI excluded myelopathy); intubation for worsening respiratory failure; rapid progression of soft-tissue lesions; death ~12 h after admission
clinical_course_record.source_text_value: Despite an escalating norepinephrine dose (>0.2 µg/kg/min) ... Urine output declined progressively ... Hypoglycemia developed ... Worsening respiratory failure necessitated endotracheal intubation ... died approximately 12 hours after admission

confirmatory_findings.finding: Blood cultures: Streptococcus pyogenes emm1 (fully susceptible); CDC criteria for confirmed STSS fulfilled
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The isolation of S. pyogenes emm1 from a normally sterile site (blood), in combination with the clinical criteria ... fulfilled the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) criteria for a confirmed diagnosis of STSS

confirmatory_findings.finding: Oral swab: S. pyogenes emm1 and non-PVL S. aureus; urine: hemolytic E. coli (not considered primary pathogen); SARS-CoV-2 PCR negative
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: An oral swab yielded both S. pyogenes carrying the emm1 gene and non-PVL-producing S. aureus ... A urine specimen grew hemolytic Escherichia coli ... A SARS-CoV-2 PCR test was negative.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Autopsy: polymicrobial meningitis (N. meningitidis serogroup C, S. pyogenes, hemolytic E. coli) attributed to terminal translocation; left chest wall phlegmon and early lung changes due to S. pyogenes; discrete colitis; previously undiagnosed lymphoproliferative disorder (renal infiltration, generalized lymphadenopathy, hypercellular marrow)
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Postmortem microbiological evaluation ... revealed a polymicrobial infection ... the autopsy also revealed a previously undiagnosed lymphoproliferative disorder

outcome.source_text_value: the patient deteriorated rapidly and died approximately 12 hours after admission from refractory septic shock and fulminant multiorgan failure

quality_warnings: Primary diagnosis per paper is STSS (CDC-confirmed); Streptococcus pyogenes bacteremia and the soft-tissue phlegmon are components of the same illness. Necrotizing fasciitis was a differential but not diagnosed (autopsy: phlegmon).

Postmortem meningococcal/polymicrobial meningitis and the autopsy-discovered lymphoproliferative disorder are non-ranking (not known at presentation; authors attribute meningitis to terminal translocation).
CT 2 h after admission is treated as same-day presentation imaging; the admission chest radiograph (no infiltrate) is record-only on the same axis.
GCS reported as 13-14 in the SOFA table (midpoint used) while the narrative says conscious and oriented.
Differential counts converted to absolute counts; urea, creatinine, CK and bilirubin converted from SI units (conversions recorded per item).
